content:
Someone you invite will often watch a clip before they agree to come. Use that clip to help them take a local next step. A Vision Meeting. A conversation. Launch Sunday, once you have announced the date, time, and place.

Public video before launch supports those invitations. It does not stand in for the gathering, and it is not a live broadcast of your practice services. Count the people who come. Do not count the people who press play.

---

## What public video is for

You are asking neighbors to meet you in a room. A clip can show the Senior Pastor, a few people from the Launch Team, and the place you will meet. It should name one next step and stop there.

For Core Group growth, that next step is a Vision Meeting. [Invitation Strategies](/wiki/core-group/vision-meetings/invitation-strategies) still starts with a personal conversation. The clip follows the conversation. It does not replace it. Closer to Launch Sunday, the next step is the service you have announced.

Do not build an online audience and call it progress. A neighbor who watches and never comes has not joined the Core Group, the Launch Team, or a service.

<Callout type="important">
Barna's figures below come from a survey of U.S. adults collected April 28 to May 5, 2020. Lifeway Research's figures come from a survey of Protestant churchgoers collected September 19 to 29, 2022. Those figures describe people who already had a church connection. They are not a forecast for your city, and they are not a launch target.
</Callout>

Lifeway Research asked those churchgoers about livestreams. 20 percent said a livestream is how they get to know a new church before visiting in person. Fewer than 3 in 10 said a livestream is a valid replacement when a non-attendee wants to know more about the church or its teaching. A full service online is a weak introduction. A short clip with a local ask fits better.

In Barna's spring 2020 study, some churched adults saw online worship as a chance to invite friends to visit their church online. Barna reported 22 percent for Christian friends and 14 percent for friends who are not Christians. A clip can travel with an invitation. It still needs a room at the end of it. In that same survey, only 30 percent of practicing Christians said they had contact with a church leader in the last month. Watching did not produce the conversation a Vision Meeting is for.

<Callout type="insight">
A view, a comment, or a share is not attendance. It is not a completed Vision Meeting. Everyfield does not count those numbers as Vision Meeting attendance. Track who came, and who you still need to invite.
</Callout>

---

## What to publish

Record pieces on purpose. Do not cut them out of a practice service.

**People.** Show the Senior Pastor and two teammates. Close with the next Vision Meeting, including the date and place.

**Teaching.** Record a few minutes for this post, not from a rehearsal. Close with the same local ask.

**Prep.** Show the team getting ready, with no service in the frame. Close with Launch Sunday, once you have announced the date, time, and place.

[The Promotion Plan](/wiki/pre-launch/the-promotion-plan) already allows video and sermon previews in the weeks before Launch Sunday. Stay in that lane. One ask per clip. Put the date, time, and place in the video and in the text beside it.

A preparation update can show set-up, the team praying, or a walk through the neighborhood. Leave the worship set, any sermon aimed at an empty room, and children's ministry practice out of the frame. Those belong to the Launch Team. Keep a public clip short enough to send in a message. If you need ten minutes to say where you meet, the clip is doing the wrong job.

---

## What stays off the internet

[Pre-Launch Services](/wiki/pre-launch/pre-launch-services) are for the Launch Team, not guests. Record at least one and watch it with the team. Look for transitions, timing, and how the room actually looks. That recording is for learning. It is not a preview for the people you are inviting.

Do not livestream a Pre-Launch Service. Do not post it later. Do not send a private link to a friend, a partner church, or a group chat outside the team. A link is a broadcast once it leaves the people who were supposed to be in the room.

<Callout type="warning">
If you can stop the service to fix a problem, guests should not be watching. That freedom is the point of a rehearsal. Publishing the recording takes the freedom away.
</Callout>

Keep the three kinds of video apart.

**Invite clip.** For people you are asking to come. Put it on a public page or in a personal message.

**Rehearsal.** For the Launch Team only. Watch it in team review, and leave it there.

**Live service.** Not part of this launch method. Do not start one before Launch Sunday.

A weekly public teaching before Launch Sunday would be a second gathering. It would not count as a Vision Meeting, and it would change what Launch Sunday marks. After you are gathering each week, the church can decide about ongoing video. That decision is not a step on the way to launch.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"not forsaking our own assembling together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the day drawing near."* — Hebrews 10:25 (LSB)
</Callout>

---

## Send the clip with a person

Posting is not inviting. The Launch Team still has the conversation. Send the clip with the ask, not instead of it. A text that only drops a link asks them to watch. A text that names the meeting asks them to come.

You might write, "We meet Thursday at 7 at the library room on Oak Street. Here is a short look at who we are. Can I save you a seat?" Change the details. Do not change the ask.

- [ ] Name one next step, with a date, a time, and a place.
- [ ] Show people from your team, not only a logo.
- [ ] Keep the clip short enough to send in a message.
- [ ] Answer questions yourself. A comment thread is not follow-up.
- [ ] At Vision Meetings and on Launch Sunday, ask how guests heard about you. Write down names, not view counts.

<Callout type="tip">
Give one person the public posts. The [promotion leader](/wiki/launch-team/leadership/promotion-leader-role) is the natural owner. They keep the ask the same from clip to clip. Everyone else still invites in person.
</Callout>

Partner churches may want something to share. Give them the introduction clip, with the next local step on it. Do not give them the rehearsal.

---

## When someone cannot come

This use of video gives less live access to people who cannot be in the room. A parent on a night shift. A neighbor in the hospital. A friend who is out of town. A short clip and a personal message are the help you can offer before launch. Call them. Tell them the next date you hope they can come. Do not open a weekly public broadcast so they have a service to watch instead.

You are not ignoring them. You are refusing to pretend a screen is the gathering. The invitation is still to come when they can.

---

## Keep setup separate from the decision

Cameras, encoders, upload tests, and private stream tests are covered in [Streaming Equipment and Setup](/wiki/administrative/technology/streaming-equipment-and-setup). Read that when you are connecting gear. Do not read it as a reason to start public services online. A phone on a shelf is enough for an introduction clip.

If a public clip includes a song, a backing track, or a film clip, check permissions before you post. [Copyright Licenses for Worship and Streaming](/wiki/administrative/legal/copyright-licenses-for-worship-and-streaming) separates what you may do in the room from what you may put online. A song the team sings in rehearsal is not automatically cleared for a public video. When in doubt, leave the music out. Buying a streaming kit does not decide the method. Equipment can wait until you know what you will actually publish.

---

## Mistakes that blur the line

Posting a practice service "so people can see we are real" shows them a gathering you said was closed.

Counting views toward the Core Group treats a screen total as a person who has said yes. It is not.

Starting a weekly live teaching "just until launch" creates a public gathering that is not a Vision Meeting. Stop before the first one.

A music bed you did not clear can come down the week you are inviting the neighborhood. Leave it out, or get permission first.

Children's faces do not belong in a public update unless a parent has agreed to that specific clip. A shot of the room without faces is enough.

If the viewer cannot tell where to come, the clip failed, however many people watched it.

claim_check.notes: Owner review by Sebastian; no model review per his 2026-10-26 instruction.

rulings: Bryan ruled B6 = Option A: "Video supports local invitations" (2026-10-26 1:31 PM ET).

Wording: title is "Video Before You Launch" rather than the backlog title "Streaming Before You Launch", because "streaming" suggests a live broadcast, which this ruling does not choose. Slug kept as pre-launch/streaming-before-you-launch so the backlog title remains findable.

Wording: the article does not teach a regular public live broadcast, viewer-contact staffing, or an online gathering. It names the limit for people who cannot attend and points them to a personal follow-up and a later local step.
Wording: practice-service recordings stay with the Launch Team. The article does not specify a platform privacy setting. Private tests remain in Streaming Equipment and Setup.

Wording: the body does not cite REQ-PI-004 or REQ-PHASE-008. It states in planter language that views are not Vision Meeting attendance, and that Everyfield does not count them as such. No online-audience target is added.
Wording: children's faces stay out of public clips unless a parent has agreed to that specific clip. This is a prudence call, not a legal ruling.
Wording: no SBC or network-program specifics. Public sources are Barna Group and Lifeway Research only. The Playbook's rehearsal boundary is followed without quoting it.
